newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr ends steady, Aust dlr movement seen key.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr ends steady, Aust dlr movement seen key.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed steady on Monday, practically unchanged from its local open after a quiet session.
Dealers said the currency felt reasonably firm and saw it moving higher as the week progressed.

"It still continues to hold that US$0.6860 level quite well. That's the all important level -- if we broke that support we could see the low 0.6800s tested pretty quickly," said a Wellington chief dealer.
The Kiwi closed at US$0.6885/95 and at 68.17 on its Trade-Weighted Index, almost unchanged from its 0.6883/90 and 68.15 open. It traded a 0.6887-98 range during the session.
Dealers said the key issue for the Kiwi was now the Australian dollar.
"Clearly the market feels the Aussie is going lower, and that's sort of hanging over the head of the Kiwi right now," said the chief dealer.
"The big negative for the Aussie is this ongoing talk of another rate cut in Australia.
"On balance this week I think the Kiwi is going to do quite well as I favour the Aussie to retrace a lot of its losses from last week.

"I don't think we will get a rate cut in Australia and I think we'll see the Aussie move back towards the 0.7675, maybe even 0.7700 level as the week progresses, and I think we'll see Kiwi back above 69 (US) cents," he said.
Tuesday's Household Labour Force Survey would be watched with interest.

"I think the market will be looking towards that number initially to give us a cue as to what the economic environment is like out there at the moment, but unless it's way outside expectations, I don't think we'll see a major currency move on the back of it," a dealer said.
Economists polled by Reuters expect 0.325 percent employment growth for the December quarter.
